\begin{abstract}
Chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability, a model's ability to follow instructions about its own reasoning, matters for CoT monitoring because it correlates with the ability to obfuscate reasoning. We ask whether ordinary supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on benign reasoning data, with no controllability objective, can raise it. We fine-tune Qwen3-14B, Phi-4-reasoning, and OLMo-3-7B-Think on 212 GPT-5.2 reasoning summaries of software-engineering requests and evaluate them on ReasonIF and on the seven CoT-Control tasks that predict obfuscation. In Qwen3-14B, ReasonIF instruction-following success rises from 14.0\% to 33.3\% (33.7\% and 33.0\% for two further training seeds), and CoT-Control compliance rises from 13.55 to 19.02--19.77; the CoT-Control gain survives scoring only the first 100 words and scoring degenerate outputs as failures, and ReasonIF accuracy falls from 80.3\% to 59.3--65.3\%. Ten tokens written by the fine-tuned model raise the unchanged base model's CoT-Control compliance by 6.87 points. The teacher matters: on the same 212 questions, raw reasoning from Claude 3.7 Sonnet raises CoT-Control compliance by 7.43 points, while reasoning from DeepSeek R1 does not. In Phi-4-reasoning the gain is explained by shorter outputs, and OLMo-3-7B-Think shows none. Ordinary distillation can therefore raise controllability, which should be re-measured after post-training.

\section{Conclusion}
Supervised fine-tuning on 212 benign GPT-5.2 reasoning summaries raised measured CoT controllability in Qwen3-14B, on ReasonIF and on the seven CoT-Control tasks that predict obfuscation, consistently across three training seeds and beyond what shorter outputs or degenerate text explain, and ten tokens written by the fine-tuned model transfer much of the CoT-Control gain to the unchanged base model. Which teacher wrote the training reasoning matters: with the same questions, raw reasoning from Claude 3.7 Sonnet raises controllability and reasoning from DeepSeek R1 does not. The summaries' opening headings matter as well, but they account for the case tasks better than for the tasks that predict obfuscation, where what carries the effect remains open. The effect is model-dependent: it is explained by shorter outputs in Phi-4-reasoning and absent in OLMo-3-7B-Think. Controllability should be re-measured after ordinary distillation, not assumed to fall.
